explanation: Moving a lead pointer k links ahead creates a fixed k-link gap. Advancing both pointers together preserves that gap; when the lead falls off the end, the trailing pointer has exactly k nodes including itself left to the tail.
correctness: Nonpositive k cannot name a one-based position. If the lead reaches null before k advances, the list is too short. Otherwise the lead stays exactly k links ahead of the trailing pointer throughout the joint walk. At termination its position is one past the tail, so the trailing pointer is exactly kth from the tail and is an original node. No links or values are changed.
walkthrough: For [4,7,7,9] and k=2, advance the lead from index 0 to index 2. Joint steps move the pair to (3,1), then (null,2). Return the original node at index 2, whose value is 7; the equal-valued node at index 1 is not the answer.
timeComplexity: O(n) time, including out-of-range k: the lead walk stops at null rather than performing k unchecked steps.
edgeCases: Empty input and all nonpositive k return null.
k=1 selects the tail; k=n selects the head.
